topics.title: Changing the subject of a formula

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = x + 5\]
questions.hint: Undo addition: subtract 5 from both sides.

steps.explain: Start with the given formula. The subject we want is \(x\), currently on the right with \(+5\).
Subtract 5 from both sides to undo the addition. Whatever you do to one side you must do to the other.
Write with \(x\) as the subject (swap sides if you prefer).

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = x - 3\]
questions.hint: Undo subtraction: add 3 to both sides.

steps.explain: Given formula. \(x\) has 3 subtracted from it.
Add 3 to both sides to undo the subtraction.

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = 4x\]
questions.hint: Undo multiplication: divide both sides by 4.

steps.explain: Divide both sides by 4 to isolate \(x\).

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = \dfrac{x}{6}\]
questions.hint: Undo division: multiply both sides by 6.

steps.explain: The right-hand side is now just \(x\).

questions.stem:
Make \(q\) the subject of the formula:
\[p = q - r\]
questions.hint: Add \(r\) to both sides.
questions.solution: Add \(r\) to both sides: \(q = p + r\).

steps.explain: Add \(r\) to both sides to cancel \(-r\).

questions.stem:
Make \(n\) the subject of the formula:
\[m = n + k\]
questions.hint: Subtract \(k\) from both sides.
questions.solution: Subtract \(k\) from both sides: \(n = m - k\).

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = 2x + 7\]
questions.hint: First subtract 7, then divide by 2.

steps.explain: Given formula. Undo operations in reverse order (opposite of BODMAS).

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = 5x - 3\]
questions.hint: Add 3 first, then divide by 5.

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = 3(x + 4)\]
questions.hint: Divide by 3 first (to remove the brackets), then subtract 4.

steps.explain: Given formula. The brackets mean everything inside is multiplied by 3.

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = 4(x - 2) + 1\]
questions.hint: Subtract 1, divide by 4, then add 2.

steps.explain: Add 2 to both sides to isolate \(x\).

questions.stem:
Make \(t\) the subject of the formula:
\[v = u + at\]
questions.hint: Subtract \(u\), then divide by \(a\).

steps.explain: This is the linear motion formula relating final velocity \(v\), initial velocity \(u\), acceleration \(a\) and time \(t\).

questions.stem:
Make \(u\) the subject of the formula:
\[v = u + at\]
questions.hint: Subtract \(at\) from both sides.

steps.explain: Given the motion formula, isolate initial velocity \(u\).
The right-hand side is now just \(u\).

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = \dfrac{x}{a} + b\]
questions.hint: Subtract \(b\), then multiply by \(a\).

questions.stem:
The average of two numbers \(m\) and \(n\) is given by
\[a = \dfrac{m + n}{2}\]
Make \(m\) the subject.
questions.hint: Multiply by 2, then subtract \(n\).

steps.explain: The average sits halfway between \(m\) and \(n\) on the number line.
Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the fraction.

questions.stem:
Make \(u\) the subject of the formula:
\[v = \dfrac{u}{t}\]
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by \(t\).

steps.explain: This is the speed formula \(v = \dfrac{u}{t}\) (distance over time).

questions.stem:
The thin-lens formula is
\[\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{v}\]
Make \(f\) the subject.
questions.hint: Combine the right-hand side over a common denominator, then take the reciprocal.

steps.explain: Given the thin-lens formula. \(f\) is focal length, \(u\) object distance, \(v\) image distance.
Combine the right-hand side with common denominator \(uv\).
Take the reciprocal of both sides (flip both fractions).
So the focal length is the product of the distances over their sum.

questions.stem:
Given
\[\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{v}\]
Make \(u\) the subject.
questions.hint: Isolate \(\dfrac{1}{u}\), then take the reciprocal.

steps.explain: Start from the thin-lens formula and isolate the term with \(u\).
Take the reciprocal of both sides.

questions.stem:
The area of a rectangle is \(A = lw\).
Make \(l\) the subject.
questions.hint: Divide both sides by the width \(w\).

steps.explain: Area of a rectangle equals length times width.
The right-hand side is the length.

questions.stem:
The area of a triangle is \(A = \dfrac{1}{2}bh\).
Make \(h\) the subject.
questions.hint: Multiply by 2, then divide by \(b\).

steps.explain: Area of a triangle is half base times height.
Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the fraction.
Divide both sides by the base \(b\).

questions.stem:
The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^{2}\).
Make \(r\) the subject (take the positive root).
questions.hint: Divide by \(\pi\), then take the square root.

steps.explain: Area of a circle with radius \(r\).
Take the positive square root of both sides (radius is positive).
Final form with \(r\) as the subject.

questions.stem:
The circumference of a circle is \(C = 2\pi r\).
Make \(r\) the subject.
questions.hint: Divide both sides by \(2\pi\).

questions.stem:
The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^{2} h\).
Make \(h\) the subject.
questions.hint: Divide both sides by the base area \(\pi r^{2}\).

steps.explain: Volume of a cylinder = base area \(\times\) height.
The right-hand side is the height.

questions.stem:
The volume of a cone is \(V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^{2} h\).
Make \(r\) the subject (take the positive root).
questions.hint: Multiply by 3, divide by \(\pi h\), then take the square root.

steps.explain: Volume of a cone is one-third the volume of the enclosing cylinder.

questions.stem:
The area of a trapezium is \(A = \dfrac{1}{2}(a + b)h\).
Make \(h\) the subject.
questions.hint: Multiply by 2, then divide by \((a + b)\).

steps.explain: Trapezium area uses the average of the parallel sides times the height.

questions.stem:
The perimeter of a rectangle is \(P = 2(l + w)\).
Make \(w\) the subject.
questions.hint: Divide by 2, then subtract \(l\). (Equivalent form: \(w = \dfrac{P - 2l}{2}\).)

steps.explain: Perimeter is twice the sum of length and width.

questions.stem:
A stone is thrown from a cliff. The distance fallen is
\[s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}\]
Make \(u\) the subject.
questions.hint: Subtract \(\tfrac{1}{2}at^{2}\), then divide by \(t\). Simplify \(\dfrac{\tfrac{1}{2}at^{2}}{t} = \tfrac{1}{2}at\).

steps.explain: Displacement formula with initial speed \(u\) and constant acceleration \(a\).
Subtract \(\dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}\) from both sides to isolate the \(ut\) term.

questions.stem:
Given the formula
\[v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as\]
Make \(a\) the subject.
questions.hint: Subtract \(u^{2}\), then divide by \(2s\).

steps.explain: This motion formula links speeds and displacement without time.

questions.stem:
The Fahrenheit–Celsius conversion is
\[F = \dfrac{9}{5}C + 32\]
Make \(C\) the subject.
questions.hint: Subtract 32, then multiply by \(\dfrac{5}{9}\).

steps.explain: Temperature conversion formula from Celsius to Fahrenheit.
Multiply both sides by \(\dfrac{5}{9}\) (the reciprocal of \(\dfrac{9}{5}\)).

questions.stem:
Kinetic energy is given by
\[E = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\]
Make \(v\) the subject (take the positive root).
questions.hint: Multiply by 2, divide by \(m\), then take the square root.

steps.explain: Kinetic energy of a mass \(m\) moving at speed \(v\).
Take the positive square root (speed is non-negative).

questions.stem:
Simple interest is given by
\[I = \dfrac{PRT}{100}\]
Make \(T\) the subject.
questions.hint: Multiply by 100, then divide by \(PR\).

steps.explain: Simple interest \(I\) depends on principal \(P\), rate \(R\)% and time \(T\).

questions.stem:
The surface area of a rectangular prism is
\[S = 2(lw + lh + hw)\]
Make \(h\) the subject.
questions.hint: Expand, isolate terms with \(h\), then factor \(h\).
questions.solution: \(\dfrac{S}{2} = lw + h(l + w)\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(h(l + w) = \dfrac{S}{2} - lw\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(h = \dfrac{S - 2lw}{2(l + w)}\).

steps.explain: Total surface area of a rectangular box with dimensions \(l\), \(w\), \(h\).
Divide by 2, then expand and group the terms that contain \(h\).
Divide by \((l + w)\) and rewrite the left side with common denominator 2: \(\dfrac{S - 2lw}{2(l + w)}\).

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = \sqrt{\dfrac{x}{a}}\]
questions.hint: Square both sides, then multiply by \(a\).

steps.explain: Given formula with a square root.
Square both sides to remove the square root.

questions.stem:
By Pythagoras,
\[c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\]
Make \(a\) the subject (take the positive root).
questions.hint: Subtract \(b^{2}\), then take the square root.

steps.explain: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
Take the positive square root (length is positive).
Final form with \(a\) as the subject.

questions.stem:
The period of a simple pendulum is
\[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}\]
Make \(l\) the subject.
questions.hint: Divide by \(2\pi\), square both sides, then multiply by \(g\).

steps.explain: Period \(T\) depends on length \(l\) and gravity \(g\).

questions.stem:
Make \(x\) the subject of the formula:
\[y = \dfrac{ax + b}{cx + d}\]
questions.hint: Cross-multiply, collect terms with \(x\) on one side, then factor.
questions.solution: \(y(cx + d) = ax + b\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(cxy - ax = b - dy\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(x(cy - a) = b - dy\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(x = \dfrac{dy - b}{a - cy}\).

steps.explain: Start with a linear fractional formula. Multiply both sides by the denominator.
Collect terms with \(x\) on the left and constants on the right: subtract \(ax\) and subtract \(dy\).
steps.work: \(cxy - ax = b - dy\)\n\(x(cy - a) = b - dy\)

steps.explain: Divide by \((cy - a)\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(-1\) gives the equivalent form \(\dfrac{dy - b}{a - cy}\).

questions.stem:
The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^{2}\).
Rearrange to make \(r\) the subject, then find \(r\) when \(A = 50\) (use \(\pi = 3.14\), correct to 2 decimal places).

steps.explain: Rearrange: divide by \(\pi\) and take the positive square root.
Take the square root and round to 2 decimal places.

questions.stem: Using \(v = u + at\), make \(t\) the subject and find \(t\) when \(v = 30\), \(u = 10\), \(a = 4\).

steps.explain: Rearrange for time: subtract \(u\), divide by \(a\).

questions.stem: Using \(F = \dfrac{9}{5}C + 32\), make \(C\) the subject and convert \(F = 86\) to Celsius.

A triangle has area \(A = 48\text{ cm}^{2}\) and base \(b = 12\text{ cm}\).
Using \(A = \dfrac{1}{2}bh\), find the height \(h\).
questions.hint: \(h = \dfrac{2A}{b} = \dfrac{2 \times 48}{12}\).

steps.explain: Rearrange the triangle area formula for height.

questions.stem: Make \(x\) the subject of the formula \(y=6x-5\).
questions.hint: Add \(5\) to both sides first, then divide by \(6\).

steps.explain: Add \(5\) to both sides to isolate the term containing \(x\).

meta.source: Sydney Grammar School Form III Annual Examination 2022

questions.stem: If \(bx+5d=ax+2c\), then \(x\) is equal to which of the expressions below?
questions.hint: Collect all the \(x\) terms on one side, then factorise and divide.

steps.explain: Move all \(x\) terms to one side and all other terms to the other side.
Divide both sides by \((b-a)\), then multiply top and bottom by \(-1\) to match the answer format.

meta.source: Sydney Grammar School Form III Annual Examination 2022

questions.stem: Find an expression for \(b\) given \(\dfrac{2a+1}{b}+\dfrac1c=\dfrac13\). Express your answer as a single fraction.
questions.hint: Isolate the term containing \(b\) first, then take the reciprocal of both sides.

steps.explain: Subtract \(\dfrac1c\) from both sides to isolate the term containing \(b\).
Combine the right-hand side into a single fraction over the common denominator \(3c\).
So \(\dfrac{2a+1}{b}=\dfrac{c-3}{3c}\). Take the reciprocal of both sides, then multiply both sides by \((2a+1)\).

meta.source: Sydney Grammar School Form III Annual Examination 2022

questions.stem: Change the subject of the formula to \(r\): \(V = \pi r^2 h\)
questions.hint: Isolate r² first by dividing, then take the square root.

steps.explain: Divide both sides by πh to isolate r².
Take the square root of both sides.

questions.stem: Consider the following equation: \(s = \frac{a}{1 - r}\). Change the subject to \(r\).
Change the subject of the formula to \(r\): \(V = \pi r^2 h\)

steps.explain: Divide both sides by \(\pi h\) to isolate the term with \(r\).
Take the square root of both sides to make \(r\) the subject. Since \(r\) represents a length (the radius of a cylinder), it must be positive.
